key_insight: LongAgent introduces a history-guided agentic search strategy to better predict future outcomes from longitudinal medical data. Instead of treating all variables equally, it focuses on the most informative past measurements and their temporal context to build stronger predictive representations.
problem_solved: The paper addresses the challenge of making accurate predictions from heterogeneous longitudinal healthcare data, where variables come from different sources, are sampled at irregular intervals, and may vary in predictive usefulness over time.
method: Uses an agentic search process to explore longitudinal histories and identify informative variables and time segments.
Guides representation learning with past patient history so the model can prioritize clinically relevant signals over noisy or redundant measurements.
Integrates multi-source, irregularly sampled medical variables into a unified representation for future outcome prediction.
impact: This matters for AI/ML practitioners because it offers a practical way to handle messy real-world time series data, especially in healthcare. It can improve prediction quality while making models more selective and interpretable about which historical evidence they rely on.
visual_elements: A pipeline diagram showing raw longitudinal EHR data flowing into history-guided search and then into outcome prediction.
A timeline visualization with irregular patient measurements highlighted by importance scores.
An agent/search tree illustrating how the model selects relevant variables and past events.
A comparison chart showing improved prediction performance versus standard sequence models.
paper_title: LongAgent: History-Guided Agentic Search for Longitudinal Outcome Prediction
paper_authors: Siyao Wang, Florian Guitton, Shuojie Fu, Guanyu Tao, Kai Sun
